name: Magnetic Field
description: Dipole-based energy field maintaining spatial coherence through aligned spin and flux stabilization.

core_attributes.pattern: dipole attraction, spin symmetry, field stabilization

scope.definition: Magnetic flux conservation through a superconducting loop — fractional drift in quantized flux (Φ₀ = h/2e = 2.068×10⁻¹⁵ Wb) over 1 year at 4K, measured by SQUID magnetometry.

evidence.source: Jaklevic et al. (1964) 'Quantum interference effects in Josephson tunneling', Physical Review Letters 12:159-160; File & Mills (1963) 'Observation of persistent current in a superconducting solenoid', Physical Review Letters 10:93-96.
cross_domain_examples: persistent current in lead ring at 4K: flux unchanged to 1 part in 10¹⁵ over 2+ years (File & Mills 1963)
SQUID magnetometer: flux quantum resolution h/2e — most sensitive magnetic measurement device
Earth's magnetic field: slow secular variation 0.1%/year — contrast to superconducting perfection

scope.falsifiability: If measured flux in a superconducting loop drifts by more than 10⁻¹⁰ Φ₀ per year at 4K below Tc, flux quantization and conservation are not operating as described.
scope.measurement_limits: Perfect flux conservation requires temperature below Tc (superconducting transition). Normal-state magnetic flux is not conserved — flux diffuses through resistive material. Measurement requires careful thermal isolation.
